Uomo di 66 anni. PSA 11,9 ng/mL; volume: 66-year-old man. PSA 11.9 ng/mL; prostate volume about 132 mL (PSA density about 0.09 ng/mL²). Prostate MRI at 3 T (axial T2, calculated high-b diffusion and ADC map).
Referta: zona periferica, zona di transi: Report: peripheral zone, transition zone, conclusion.
Saper dire «negativo» è una competenza q:
Being able to say "negative" is as much a skill as finding the tumor. In the normal peripheral zone, T2 is uniformly bright and at high b there are no focal bright areas with dark ADC. The transition zone enlarged by hypertrophy has well-encapsulated nodules with mixed signal and an "organized mosaic" appearance: it must not be mistaken for tumor (in the transition zone the deciding sequence is T2, not diffusion).
PSA density = PSA / prostate volume: below 0.10-0.15 ng/mL² the risk of clinically significant cancer with a negative MRI is low, and biopsy can often be avoided (shared decision with the urologist).
Here the "high" PSA (12) depends on the volume: 132 mL gives a density of about 0.09. The median lobe protruding into the bladder must not be mistaken for a bladder tumor: on sagittal images or scrolling through the axial slices it is in continuity with the gland.
PSA alto in prostata enorme: calcola la: High PSA in a huge prostate: calculate the PSA density. Median lobe in the bladder = prostate, not bladder tumor.
